decisions.name: the remark that for semisimple g the invariants functor is exact, so H^i(g,V)=H^i(g,C) tensor V^g
decisions.reason: This concerns coefficients in a semisimple Lie algebra and is already published at DG-29 through the Whitehead lemmas; RL-11 treats the nilpotent radical, where the invariants functor is not exact.
decisions.evidence: Step 8 serial review. Current page library/lie-theory/lie-algebra-cohomology-and-kostants-nilradical-theorem.md and batch-25.pages.json retain 13 items, including thm-casselman-osborne-nilradical-cohomology-constraint, thm-kostant-nilradical-cohomology-theorem. Woit compares cohomology with trivial-coefficient cohomology using exact invariants in the finite-dimensional semisimple/compact context. Exactness is false on arbitrary U(g)-modules (for g=sl2 the augmentation U(g)->C has no invariant lift: left multiplication by a nonzero Lie algebra element is injective in U(g), so the regular module has no nonzero invariants), and Whitehead H1/H2 vanishing alone is not the stated all-degree tensor formula. The nilradical items do not need this result, but its source/claimed-published-coverage qualification needs owner reconciliation.
